actions.government_body: City of Norwalk Planning and Zoning Commission
actions.result_status: Planning and Zoning minutes describe Project West as approximately 300 acres in the Southwest Development Corridor and recommend approval of the Norwalk Technology and Industry Overlay District.
actions.access_caveat: Official commission minutes; describes recruitment/zoning process, not a data-center building permit.
actions.evidence_note: Supports local-process status and approximate project acreage.

actions.result_status: The City says the March 5 council item is an agreement with a land developer; the vote does not approve or authorize a data center, and any future data center would require separate city-level review, state/federal regulatory requirements, and public meetings.
actions.access_caveat: Official notice; does not identify a final operator or a site-plan/permit application.
actions.evidence_note: Negative/limiting government statement; no approval inferred.

actions.result_status: Council minutes state the public hearing concerned a proposed development agreement with IALCO Warren County Two, LLC to prepare property within city limits for potential future data center development; any future operator must submit site plans and comply with applicable local, state, and federal regulations. Resolution 26059 approving the development agreement carried unanimously.
actions.access_caveat: Official minutes; approval is for the development agreement and pledged tax-increment payments, not a data-center site plan or construction permit.
actions.evidence_note: Best current official evidence for status advancement from announced/under review to local process.

actions.result_status: Mayor's statement calls the southwest-edge development a project underway, estimates roughly half a billion dollars injected into the local economy, and projects $14 million to $16 million per year in new tax revenue split among the city, school district, and county, with no local tax incentives.
actions.access_caveat: Official mayoral statement; does not identify the final data center operator, MW capacity, building count, or construction authorization.
actions.evidence_note: Adds current official economic/tax framing but does not prove construction or energization.

owner: IALCO Warren County Two, LLC is the City development-agreement counterparty; industry reporting identifies Tract as the data-center park developer. Final operator/end user remains unconfirmed.

contradictions.resolution: Use local-process status, not approved-permitted or construction.
